A Dubai-based firm has sued a gold-trading company seeking a refund of more than Sh63 million it paid for the precious metal in June but was never delivered as agreed. According to a 7 January 2025 publication in Daily Nation, the Auditor-General’s report flagged unexplained expenditure of approximately KSh 147.7 million by the Kenya Water Towers Agency on a purported bamboo-planting/forest-conservation project in Kaptagat Forest — a project now described as a “ghost” initiative because there is no verifiable evidence that any meaningful work was done. This strongly suggests that public funds intended for environmental conservation were misused or misappropriated. The lack of delivery combined with absence of transparency points to either gross mismanagement or deliberate diversion of funds. The motive appears to be enrichment or benefit of insiders under the guise of a conservation project, facilitated by weak oversight. Because KWTA was dissolved in December 2024 (after its founding legal instrument expired), the institutional restructuring may muddy the waters in terms of accountability, asset traceability, and follow-up on what happened to funds.

Investigations have implicated senior officials including former PS Susan Mochache and suspended KNH CEO Evanson Kamuri, while Novair SAS, the French subcontractor, demands unpaid dues. The case exposes deep procurement irregularities, corruption, and governance failures in Kenya’s health sector.

The article unveils a serious illicit trade in human organs, notably kidneys, in the North Rift region of Kenya. The organ trade is illegal and strictly prohibited by law, but loopholes and poor enforcement persist. Victims suffer severe health consequences post-operation, with some left sickly and uncompensated. Investigations and parliamentary inquiries are ongoing, emphasizing the urgent need for stronger regulations and enforcement to halt this human exploitation.

A retired diplomat, Marcellus Lazima Chege, was sentenced to one month in civil jail after repeatedly ignoring a court order requiring him to pay a KSh 6.4 million debt to a businessman. Police are seeking to charge Peter Muhia Njenga with the murder of a security guard killed during a February robbery at a Juja liquor store. Njenga is also suspected to be the mastermind of a gang responsible for over 13 break-ins across the Nairobi Metropolitan area, where alcohol worth more than Sh50 million was stolen. Several of his suspected accomplices have already been arrested and charged with robbery with violence and murder, while Njenga has repeatedly evaded arrest, including during a police raid on November 8. Investigators link him to the gang through surveillance, his unexplained cash flow, and information from a Ngara bar where the group frequently met. Police say they will charge him with murder and robbery with violence once apprehended.

Detectives in Salgaa, Nakuru, are investigating three killings of elderly people within two weeks. The latest victim, Margaret Wambui (65), was found dead in her home with severe head injuries and signs of a violent struggle. Her house had been ransacked, and several items were stolen. Earlier, an elderly couple, Joseph Ndegwa Kihiti (90) and Rose Wanjiku (63), were murdered in their home at Rigogo Farm with similar blunt-force injuries. The repeated attacks have created fear among residents, who believe a serial killer or gang may be targeting elderly people. DCI officers are pursuing multiple leads to determine whether the murders are connected and to arrest the suspects.

Police in Nairobi have arrested six members of a sophisticated criminal syndicate believed to be responsible for over 180 house break-ins across the city's affluent estates. The gang used a high-end vehicle with fake plates to gain access to gated communities and relied on female accomplices who posed as domestic workers to scout targets. The arrest of the multi-national group, including an alleged Indian ringleader, is considered a major breakthrough after a two-year crime spree.

DCI officers arrested two suspects linked to the Kwa Binzaro cult in Kilifi after more than five months on the run. Kenya continues to record rising cases of GBV, affecting women across all social classes, from low-income families to high-profile households. Despite stronger laws, the impact remains low due to entrenched cultural norms that promote male dominance and toxic masculinity from a young age. Recent cases involving relatives such as boyfriends, brothers, and cousins highlight how GBV is deeply rooted in society. Global data shows one in three women experiences violence, a trend reflected in Kenya. The article calls for early GBV education in schools, financial empowerment for women, and better understanding of abuse within the justice system to reduce GBV cases.

Rachel Adhiambo travelled to Nakuru to attend the graduation of a colleague’s daughter at Kabarak University before joining her family for Christmas in Got Agulu, Siaya County. Throughout the trip, she remained in regular contact with her elder sister, Maureen Atieno, sharing photographs and updates on her whereabouts.After the ceremony, Ms Adhiambo secured a lift in a private car from Nakuru to Kisumu, keeping her family informed throughout. She arrived in Kisumu around 10pm. Despite the late hour, she chose to continue to Bondo Town, determined to reach home the same night. Her family arranged to pick her up near Equity Bank, a well-lit area, before she would take a taxi to Usenge Market, about 25 kilometres away, where she would be collected. At around 11pm, Ms Adhiambo called her sister to confirm she had reached Bondo but could not find transport onward. Moments later, she informed her she had decided to hire a boda boda operator as it was getting late.By dawn, Ms Adhiambo’s phone remained unreachable. Family members retraced her last known movements and sought information from friends. On Saturday morning, passers- by discovered a woman’s body in Magawa, Sakwa, roughly 200 metres from the Bondo– Usenge road, and alerted authorities. Rushing to Bondo, the family found no hospital record matching her description. Her fiancé, Peter Adulo, identified her at the morgue. The Bondo sub-county police commander confirmed the incident and stated that investigations have been commenced and that the bodaboda rider was the prime suspect.

Residents and boda boda riders of Makutano Town Kapenguria in West Pokot County protest the murder of a 45 yr old boda boda rider - Gerorge Cheptot, He had dropped a passenger at Chepareria from  Makutano Town when another passanger requested to be ferried to Salaga and while on transit the passanger attacked him with an arrow killing him on the spot. Riders criticize the security forces for failing to curb insecurities.

Reports of patient fraud in Moi Teachers and Refferal Hospital Eldoret  as investigators discover patients had been making payments while believing the transaction reflected in e-Citizen government accounts as they even recieved reciepts but some portion of the payment got syphoned from the payment platform with the assistance of hospital staff.  Jane Wangari Wachira in with an outsider Khamisi Hussein Akida used her access into the billing e-Citizen platform and cleared billings without depositing any payment. The scheme had been going on for 13 months making away with sh. 10M. The lead investigator Edwin Chirchir cited the scheme could involve more perpetrators as the technical hack would have raised alarm.

KUPPET and KNUT are reported to demand for immediate arrest and prosecution of a parent (Meru's Senetor Kathuri Muringi Driver) who visited Nkubu High School and assaulted the deputy principal Nweton Gitari in claims that his son went missing after being sent home from school following disciplinary actions.

A police officer was shot dead and four others injured after armed robbers raided the Nyalenya Police Patrol Base in Kakamega. The attackers pretended to report a stolen motorcycle before launching the assault. During the attack, they shot the officer at the report office and fired at the others. They stole two rifles, each loaded with 20 rounds of ammunition, and used crowbars to break into a steel box to access the firearms.

A man identified as Abdul Mohamed attacked worshippers with a machete during early morning prayers at Westlands Mosque, Nairobi. Worshippers overpowered and disarmed him before police arrested and handed him to the Anti-Terror Police Unit (ATPU)
Reports of continued extortion by traffic police officers along jogoo rd doubting EACC commitment to eroding corruption.

A man accused of trafficking Kenyans to Russia to fight in the Ukraine war has been remanded for 14 more days. Magistrate Gideon Kiage ordered the extension to determine if the accused, Festus Omwamba, qualifies for bail. The court lacks evidence of Omwamba's place of abode and social ties, making it unclear if he meets bail requirements. A WhatsApp message allegedly confessing to breaking the law influenced the decision. The magistrate also directed a social inquiry into Omwamba's societal connections.

Frida Tololo was arraigned in an Eldoret court for allegedly distributing counterfeit alcohol and using fake VAT stamps to evade taxes amounting to over Sh278,000. She was apprehended by DCI detectives at Tarakwa Trading Centre.

The Director of Public Prosecution (DPP) has approved the prosecution of Samuel Mugo, a senior state prosecutor based in Makadara. Kiarie is accused of demanding a bribe of Sh 30,000 from Elly Mukosero to withdraw a criminal case that had stalled due to a lack of witnesses. Following the demand, the EACC conducted an investigation and laid a trap, leading to the current charges.

Justice Mboya has sentenced three high ranking Isiolo County officials to six months in jail for contempt of court. The officials failed to comply with a November 2025 court order mandating the payment of sh 3.9 million to a law firm. The judge emphasized that court orders are mandatory directives, not suggestions and hence ordered county police commander to arrest the offfials immediately to serve their sentences.

Residents of Bungoma county have supported investigations by the EACC into Catherine wambilianga over alleged corruption linked to tenders funded by the National Government Affirmative Action Fund. The probe focuses on suspected conflict of interest and money laundering involving companies awarded tenders during the 2022-2024 financial years. Residents have called foa a transparent and thorough investigations.
The perpetrator Dickens Otieno alias Mapesa stormed a children's home with a group armed with pangas and machetes , destroying part of the fence and causing panic among children.

The murder of 24 yr old Joseph Owino-Journalist found dumped while badly mutulated near Kihoto primary school in Naivasha, initial investigations pointed out that the incident was evoked from a love triangle and he had recieved threats from politician-cum-trader.

Four Kenyan nationals of British origin appeared before a court in Mombasa charged with multiple offences related to the alleged fraudulent disposal of trust property worth more than KSh 600 million located at diani Beach. The accused—Annelise Lulu Archer Clark, John Christopher Clark, Hellen Kay Hartley, and Richard Hartley denied charges of conspiracy to defraud, fraudulent disposal of trust property, obtaining land titles by false pretences, and perjury.

Kenyan authorities are seeking to revoke the refugee status of Turkish businessman Osman Erdinc Elsek,who is a fugitive from Turkey where he is wanted for fraud and document forgery.In kenya he has faced multiple investigations over the years involving threats, assault, and other alleged offences.

Weapon: Crude weapons, knives and metal rodes
Case Summary: A group of goons sormed into the hotel and broke windows, overturn furniture and looted electronics and expensive alcohol. They also attacked and tied up a female security guard and harassed and injured several hotel staff memebrs. The hotel owner Irungu Nyakera used his licence firarm to scare the attackers away. While he wasn't hurt he and his team were left shaken.

A man believed to be a member of a cybercrime syndicate who police say was found with two passports and eight national identity cards has been charged with stealing Sh200 million from a company and a financial institution.

A driver has reported that a matatu he was driving was maliciously damaged after a lady smashed the windscrreen using a stone.Further investigations have revealed that thre driver and the lady are in a relationship and were disputing over taking the child to school.

Residents of Teso South and Nambale constituencies in Busia County experienced a series of brutal killings. Five-night guards and a businessman were murdered in separate but similar attacks. One night guard was killed at Kotur Market, and another was murdered along with a businessman in Nambale town.

Four individuals were charged with carrying out a series of armed robberies across Limuru, Gitaru, Rironi, Wanguige, and parts of Nairobi. These robberies occurred hours before the assassination of Kabete MP George Muchai, though the court clarified the ruling did not relate to the murder case itself. The robbers used pistols and improvised weapons to threaten victims and steal items including cash and mobile phones.

There are reports of major fraud operation centered at Harambee House, the Office of the President in Nairobi. A group of seven individuals was arrested after allegedly orchestrating a KSh 60 million scam. The suspects reportedly gained access to government offices and used this proximity to stage fake meetings that appeared legitimate to unsuspecting businesspeople seeking government tenders.

A peaceful protest in Nyatike, Migori county, over rising insecurity turned violent after youths reacted to the killing of an M-Pesa agent. The protesters overwhelmed police, attacked Macalder Police tsation, injured several officers including the county police commander, burned a police vehicle and houses, and damaged other vehicles using stones.

Residents of Tigania East in Meru county are facing persistent attacks from armed bandits who steal livestock and have caused loss of life. The community has appealed to the national government for urgent intervention, as the raids have led to economic hardship and food insecurity among affected families.

Leaders in West pokot have raised concerns over alleged police brutality by a Special Operations Group during a firearm recovery operation. Several civilians and leaders were reported injured, including former MP Philip Rotino. Calls have been made for an immediate investigation into the conduct of the officers involved.

Offence: Operating An Illegal Sect And Practicing Fgm
Case Summary: Police in Juja, Kiambu county raided a suspected cult shrine and arrested several members, including a suspected leader. The group is believed to have been involved in illegal activities, notably Female Genital Mutilation (FGM). Investigations are ongoing as authorities gather more evidence and warn about rising outlawed sects.

An MCA was arrested in connection with protests that led to the attack and destruction of Malcader Police Station. Protesters stormed the police station and burned down a police vehicle and destroyed 3 others. They also burned down 6 police houses.
Three people were injured after being shot with arrows along the border of Kisumu and Kericho counties as they were trying to retrieve their stolen livestock.
A 70-year-old man was arrested in Kericho County after allegedly killing his 40-year-old son, Peter Kipkoech Rono, during a domestic dispute in Ketingo Village.
A businessman, Duncan Kipchirchir Kitur, was charged in an Eldoret court for allegedly defrauding a couple of KSh 1.1 million by falsely claiming he could sell them land.
An M-Pesa attendant, Harriet Nabonwe, was shot dead during a robbery at Mundika Market in Kakamega County.

A Kenyan court found that Odhimbo Ottoman Adel Walter unlawfully earned over Sh10.9 million by holding two full-time public positions simultaneously—one at KMTC in Kisumu and another with the Homa Bay County Government.

Specific Area: Homa Bay County Department Of Health
Case Summary: An anti-corruption court found that Dr. Adel Ottoman, the Homa Bay County Public Health Director, unlawfully held two public jobs at the same time and received salaries from both. Justice Benjamin Musyoki ruled that Dr. Ottoman must repay KSh10,991,712 earned from Homa Bay County between June 2016 and August 2021.

An anti-corruption court found that Dr. Adel Ottoman, was employed full-time by KMTC Kisumu while simultaneously serving in a senior county government role and later also lecturing part-time at Great Lakes University of Kisumu. Despite being appointed County Deputy Director of Health in March 2016, he never relinquished his KMTC job and continued drawing salaries from multiple institutions.Witnesses—including a county HR officer and a bank employee—provided bank records and electronic evidence linking him to dual salary payments. The court determined that he remained a KMTC employee until May 5, 2022, when he was dismissed for desertion of duty.

Specific Area: County Government Payroll Systems (Manual and IPPD)
Case Summary: Audits conducted by the Auditor‑General across eight Rift Valley counties revealed massive payroll fraud and ghost worker schemes resulting in an estimated loss of over Sh1 billion over three years. The fraud was facilitated by irregular manual payroll systems, which enabled payments to nonexistent employees, retirees, unverified staff, and individuals lacking documentation such as appointment letters or academic qualifications.

Seven suspects were accussed of defrauding a swedish businessman of over ksh60m in a fake ambulance supply deal. The incident is believed to have occurred at Harambee House where the complainant was lead to sign an alleged multi million contract

Specific Area: Thogoto,Kikuyu campus (university of Nairobi) kwa Mathare and Kwa Jamba neighborhood
Case Summary: The Kikuyu Campus area of the University of Nairobi is experiencing a violent crime, prompting multiple warnings and a temporary recommendation for students to study from home. A mob killed a suspected phone snatcher, sparking tensions between students and the local community.
Between March 2023 and August 2023, in PingiLikani village, Chonyi, Kilifi South, Abraham Mwatsuma committed the offence of defiling and impregnating a 16‑year‑old minor.A court found him guilty.

Reports of two murders in a suspected love traingle, Triza and Omondi Jalego had gone to Obunga where they planned to spend the night unaware they had been trailed by Triza's other boyfriend - Aboy, who broke into the house and stabbed them repedeatly resulting to their death. Police are trailing the suspect who's on the run.

Joram Wataka - PA to Trans Nzoia's Senator is reported to have assaulted two Journalists George Njoroge-Media Max and Gilbert Sitiati-KTN following a screenshot post on Harambee House fraud deal that involved his boss Senator Chesang and Interior PS Raymond.

KWS officers in Trans Nzoia County sparked public outrage after allegedly shooting and killing 22-year-old Boaz Kiprop Kibet while he was collecting firewood. The incident has intesified community frustration over the Shamba System and recent cases of alleged brutality by forest and wildlife authorities. Local laeders and human rights groups are now demanding a swift investigation and the prosecution of those responsible.

A man and three accomplices were arrested for allegedly killing his wife in Isebania. The victim reportedly died while being taken to hospital after sustaining injuries from an assault. Police have launched investigations, and the suspects are awaiting arraignment in court.

Police in Nakuru conducted an intelligence-led operation that led to the arrest of a 21-year-old suspected gang leader in Gioto. The suspect, believed to head the outlawed Confirm gang linked to murders in Gioto and Kivumbini, had been in hiding for nearly a month. He was apprehended with a sword and a homemade firearm.
A 24 year old lady was attacked with acid by a hitman who was hired by her lover  which left her with injuries on heer face.

Former Cabinet Secretary Raphael Tuju was manhandled by police officers at Karen Police Station. Prior to the incident, officers had stormed his Karen residence shortly after he held a press conference explaining that he had not been abducted but had been hiding for safety reasons.

A meeting on March 9 at Entim Sidai in Karen, Nairobi, brought together Raphael Tuju, lawyer Kimani Wachira, former judge‑turned‑advocate Joseph Mutava, and businessman Thomas Awili. Tuju had recently lost a High Court ruling in a billion‑shilling commercial dispute involving his company, Dari Limited, and sought urgent legal advice.During the meeting, Tuju allegedly placed Sh1 million in cash on the table, saying it was for legal instruction fees. Shortly afterward, EACC officers raided the meeting and arrested Wachira, Mutava, and Awili, claiming an attempt to bribe a judge.

Three Somali nationals were arrested at Tana Bridge police barricade on their way to Nairobi in possession of Kenyan birth certificates. Mr. Zacharia Bashir Duale was also arrested as he facilated entry of undocumented persons.

A white landcruiser is alledged to have been seen by witnesses at the cemetery early morning of 20th march 2026 and local casual labourers were hired to dig a large pit without notifying of security agencies or obtaining standard permits. the bodies initially reported were 13 but the grave had an extra unaccounted for bodies. the nature of the dicovery was 25 children and neonates some showing signs of mutilation.
Mr. JLM a retired civil servant with a sh 1 million debt owed to his former lover. After repeated defaults,he appealed and was given a temporary relief of paying the debt.

Elizabeth Nina a 34yr old paged woman left her home for idd-ul-fitr celebration at her friends place who live less than a kilometer away.The friend claims that Nina left in the company of a man. Nina was later found bruised, dead and dumped in a nearby unfinished building on a heap of garbage.
The Senate imposed a Sh500,000 fine on Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja for contempt of the House after he repeatedly failed to appear before a Senate committee
young fishermen illegally enter a protected national park to fish despite a government ban due to toxic contamination. Driven by poverty and lack of livelihoods after displacement
Armed raiders attacked Kangogo village in Nyambene, Meru County, killing one person and stealing approximately 200 cattle.

Two-and-a-half-year-old Joy Otieno died under suspicious circumstances at a day care centre in Kitengela shortly after being dropped off by her mother. Initially reported as a choking incident, a post-mortem later revealed that she died from blunt force trauma to the head, raising serious concerns of foul play.

A Nairobi businessman was abducted by four men posing as police officers shortly after withdrawing money from Equity Bank. The suspects, armed with pistols and dressed in police uniforms, falsely accused him of drug trafficking before handcuffing and robbing him of Sh4.2 million.

A Nairobi court allowed the detention of two KDF soldiers and four civilians for 10 days over an alleged plot to rob and kill Major General George Okumu. Acting on prior intelligence, officers from the DCI intercepted the suspects at the general’s residence in Kitengela on March 25.

Police in Kuria west are searching for a man who fled after allegedly killing a 19-year-old woman in a Kehancha hotel. Authorities believe the fatal altercation was sparked by a disagreement over money. This tragedy follows a separate, recent incident in nearby Isebania where a 42-year-old woman was killed by her husband, highlighting a concerning trend of local violence.

A Tiktoker known as wamitambo is being held for an additional seven days as police investigate claims of extortion and cyber harassment. The susupect allegedly posted videos accusing a Ruiru estate company of illegally selling public land. Despite court orders being served requiring the removal of the content and suspensions of his accounts, the videos remained online, leading to additional concerns regarding contempt of court.

The death of three-year-old Faiz Faraji at Gilgil Hills Academy has sparked a demand for a thorough investigation due to conflicting accounts from school officials. Initially reported as having a fever, the child's cause of death was later changed to drowning in a school fish pond, a claim the family disputes as the body and clothes appeared clean. Despite a postmorterm citing aspiratory asphyxia, the family points to the school's failure to follow mediacl protocols and their history of past negligence as evidence that the full truth has yet to be revealed.

Authorities believe the fatal altercation was sparked by a disagreement over money. This tragedy follows a separate, recent incident in nearby Isebania where a 42-year-old woman was killed by her husband, highlighting a concerning trend of local violence.

A man impersonating an officer from the National Intelligence Service allegedly defrauded a contractor through a fake Sh15 million project in Vihiga County using forged documents and false authority. The scam was discovered when the contractor sought payment from the NGCDF office and found the project never existed. He was later arrested by the EACC while allegedly receiving a bribe.
A man was found dead under unclear circumstances after being arrested by the police who claimed that he injured himself on the cell wall.

Police in Bahati Sub‑County, Nakuru, are investigating the killing of a woman whose headless body was discovered near a quarry where she worked as a security guard. The woman had a history of domestic violence in her marriage.

Specific Area: Business premises of the dealers across the four counties
Motive: Financial gain and unfair market competition
Case Summary: The Competition Authority of Kenya (CAK) recently executed a dawn raid on six major foam mattress manufacturers and distributors across Nairobi, Machakos, Kiambu, and Kisumu. This intervention was prompted by intelligence regarding suspected cartel-like behavior, including price fixing and collusive tendering, which may be artificially inflating prices for Kenyan households. Investigators seized a wide range of forensic evidence, such as laptops, hard drives, and sales records, to determine if these firms are violating the Competition Act. CAK Director-General David Kemei emphasized that the goal is to ensure essential household goods remain affordable and that unfair trade practices do not exploit the public.

A 72-year-old Dutch national was arrested in Watamu, Kilifi County, following allegations of sexually abusing multiple underage girls. Reports indicate that approximately 21 teenage victims were involved. The suspect allegedly exploited vulnerable minors over a period of time.

Specific Area: Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology
Case Summary: The report highlights allegations that Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology awarded degrees to individuals who were never admitted or did not attend classes.
An audit by the Nairobi City County Public Service Board revealed that several senior officials were employed without proper academic qualifications.

Agricultural Development Corporation MD Tonui, ADC Secretary Rojers Karumpu, NYS Director General Joseph Kiplangat were sued and found guillty of contempt of court by members of public who cited themselves of being rightful owners to a disputed land, the three hired 50 police officers who demolished and evicted residents, violating court orders that no party would interfere with the land till a verdict was passed.

Kelvin Sigei - Chuka University 2nd year student was found dead on his bed in Rovines hostel within Ndagani in Tharaka Nithi county, it's suspected his life was taken away by the girlfriend whos body was found in Kakuzi in what is said to be suicide.
A 21 Yr old man has been arrested in Tongaren Bungoma following suspicion of stabbing his brother Joshua Wafula 24yrs to death

A Nairobi tech company CEO was found liable for sexually harassing and assaulting a junior employee through repeated inappropriate WhatsApp messages, sexually suggestive videos, and non-consensual physical advances. The employee later reported being sexually assaulted in the CEO’s car after a work-related night out. The court ruled that the CEO’s conduct crossed professional boundaries and amounted to workplace sexual harassment and gender-based violence. The employee resigned, claiming the work environment had become unbearable, and was awarded Sh1.32 million in compensation while the company’s counterclaim against her was dismissed.

Violence erupted in Chesiyo, Elgeyo Marakwet County, after a disputed burial on contested land triggered armed clashes between rival groups. The conflict led to houses, granaries, and stores being burned, while gunshots forced dozens of families to flee the area. Authorities linked the attacks to illegal firearms and ongoing land disputes, and security operations were launched to disarm suspects and restore order.

Kenyan investigators arrested senior energy officials over an alleged scheme to release substandard fuel into the market despite failed quality tests. Authorities claim the officials collaborated with oil dealers to bypass fuel safety regulations for financial and commercial gain. The scandal has exposed weaknesses in fuel oversight systems and raised concerns about corruption within Kenya’s energy sector.

The death of Carolyn Khamete, a principal at Kakamega County Polytechnic. Carolyn Khamete was reported missing in Kakamega town while delivering an important document to county finance and education offices. Three days later, Carolyn Khamete’s body was discovered along the shores of Lake Victoria in Kisumu.The family of Carolyn Khamete has raised concerns and is demanding a thorough investigation, citing inconsistencies in the postmortem report that indicated drowning. The family believes the death could be linked to threats Carolyn Khamete had previously mentioned regarding financial dealings.

A five-year-old Fardosa Katia disappeared from her home in Mukuru kwa njenga while her mother was away briefly. According to Fardosa's siblings, a known neighbour entered the house and left with the child. While police have arrested one female suspect, the family is frustrated by a lack of progress and the fact that the suspect has been moved between stations without being formally charged in court.

Two middle-aged men were lynched on Friday after alegedly raping and killing a 75-year-old woman in Isiolo Municipality. The passerby pursued the suspects, who were doused in petrol and burned beyond recognition. County Commissioner, David Kiprop condemned the act and urged the public not to take the law into their own hands.

A 75-year-old woman, Howo Kadiro Omar, was sexually assaulted by two middle-aged men while she was herding goats. In immediate retaliation, a mob of "passerby" hunted down the two suspects and burned them to death.
12 hospitals are reported to have been shutdown for defrauded SHA  by laying fraudulent claims. Among them is the Bungoma West Hospital which has been suspended for 90 days.

A  fuel scandal involving alleged importation of substandard fuel has implicated senior officials over approval letters. Investigations suggest a coordinated scheme exploiting the Middle East crisis, with arrests, resignations, and an expanding probe into a possible cartel.

The third NYS corruption scandal involves allegations that senior NYS officials and their associates embezzled about Sh2 billion through procurement fraud, fictitious contracts, and payments to companies linked to insiders. Deputy Commandant-General Nicholas Makokha and Senior Superintendent David Mbogo are central suspects in the investigation led by the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC). Investigators believe stolen funds were hidden through proxy businesses, luxury assets, and properties including a hotel in Embu County. The scandal mirrors previous NYS corruption cases that have plagued the institution over the past decade.

3 police officers were attacked and injured by mob in Kesses. The officers from DCI were acting on intelligence reports that suspected stolen goods were being held in Bayete area and they were attacked upon arrival.

Motive: Disperse protesters and protect the police post.
Case Summary: Two protesters, Henry Otieno and Jack Omenda, were shot dead in Gem–Ramula, Siaya County, during demonstrations linked to alleged forced evictions associated with Shanta Gold Kenya Limited’s mining activities. Police claimed protesters attacked a police post and damaged property, prompting officers to respond. However, a local rights group said the victims were part of a peaceful protest and accused police of opening fire without warning despite an existing court order halting evictions and mining-related relocations in the area. Investigations and an independent autopsy have been demanded.

Five individuals, including two serving Kenya Defence Forces soldiers, were charged before the Milimani Magistrate’s Court with plotting to break into the home of a senior military officer in Kitengela.
Residents of Bungoma County stormed Sang’alo Police Station after the murder of two night guards who were attacked by robbers at around 4:00 a.m. on Monday, just a few metres from the police station.

Residents of Woodley Estate in Nairobi have accused Nairobi County officials of carrying out illegal evictions in defiance of existing court orders. According to the residents, the evictions resulted in approximately 30 people being rendered homeless.

Continued series of attacks targeting passengers, pedestrians and bodaboda operators triggered a wave of mob justice Ahero town where bodaboda riders began a manhunt after identification of one of the gang members which led to a killing of 7 members of the gand group.

Bernard Cheruiyot was arrested when he went to help his brother and was charged with threatening to kill a neighbour. he died while in police custody, where he was for 2 days. the police claimed that he injured himself but the postmotern results show that he was beaten to death with his hands and feet tied and hit with either fists, kicks or a soft blunt object on his head, which was the cause of death.

A 34-year-old businessman, Fortune Muthina Kinyanzui, was abducted in Kitengela, Kajiado County, by three masked men in an incident captured on CCTV. The attackers blocked his car, forcibly removed him, handcuffed him, and bundled him into a waiting vehicle before fleeing.

A 2025 report by the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission reveals widespread corruption across Kenya, where citizens are routinely forced to pay bribes to access public services.Kakamega County recorded the highest average bribes, especially within the judiciary.

Police in Kisumu have arrested three suspects linked to a violent gang attack on Godfrey Osotsi at a coffee house in Kisumu City. The attack, captured on CCTV, showed a group of hooded assailants assaulting the senator for several minutes, leaving him injured.

A Dubai-based Australian businessman was defrauded of Sh78 million in a Nairobi-based gold scam after being lured into a fake gold deal by individuals posing as legitimate traders. The suspects used forged documents and staged transactions to convince the victim that the gold was genuine.

Chaos broke out in the Taita Taveta County Assembly after MCAs initiated leadership changes that removed key assembly leaders. Heated disagreements escalated into a physical confrontation involving several members, forcing assembly proceedings to pause while security restored order.

Motive: Opposition to nurses occupying senior roles over doctors
Case Summary: The National Nurses Association of Kenya threatened nationwide industrial action against Dadaab MP Farah Maalim after he allegedly made offensive remarks about nurses in Parliament. The association demanded a public apology within seven days, arguing that the statements undermined nurses’ qualifications and leadership roles in healthcare. The disagreement originated from a dispute over training opportunities and authority structures within the health sector.

Rirising political violence and disorder in Kenya’s Nyanza region as rival political groups allegedly use hired gangs (“goons”) to intimidate opponents and disrupt meetings.  highlights growing tensions linked to struggles for political influence ahead of future elections.

Residents and elders in Githunguri, Kiambu County, staged protests against a government-backed affordable housing project planned on land they claim is a sacred cultural shrine. Police intervened to disperse demonstrators using tear gas, causing panic and minor injuries. Community members accused authorities of ignoring public participation and attempting to seize public land, while local political leaders alleged that some groups were politically mobilizing opposition to development projects in the area.

Specific Area: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT)
Case Summary: A Chinese student, Xuaning Li, was found dead in his room at JKUAT under unclear circumstances. Police recovered assorted drugs from the scene, but no suspects or confirmed cause of death have been identified. Investigations ongoing to determine wheteher the death was natural, accidental or criminal.

A reveller Brian Mwendo, died after allegedly being assaulted by a bouncer at a Nairobi club. Police arrested ten individuals, including club staff and a manager, while the main suspect (the bouncer) remains at large. The victim succumbed to injuries after being hospitalised.

A planned political rally by Rigathi Gachagua in Kikuyu town turned violent after suspected hired goons allegedly blocked roads, attacked civilians, and robbed motorists. Police were also accused of using tear gas and live ammunition to disperse crowds and prevent the rally from proceeding. Businesses closed, transport was disrupted, and several civilians were injured or affected by the unrest. Political leaders later exchanged accusations over who was behind the violence.

The Cooperatives Tribunal temporarily lifted arrest warrants against three top officials of Kencom Cooperative Society Limited, who were accused of failing to settle a KSh 183 million debt owed to Kuscco Savings and Credit Society Limited. The officials were given three months to present a workable repayment plan. If they fail to comply, the tribunal may allow the attachment and sale of cooperative assets to recover the debt.

A tragic incident occurred in Nyeri County involving the death of a one-and-a-half-year-old child, Mary Wanjiru. The toddler had been left under the care of her 21-year-old cousin, Linet Wangechi, while her mother stepped away for less than an hour. Upon the mother’s return, the child was missing, prompting a search effort involving the suspect and local residents. However, the child’s body was later recovered from River Gura two days after her disappearance.Linet Wangechi subsequently confessed to the crime, admitting that she had thrown the child into the river.

Steven Okoth confesses to the police about his involvement in the murder of a 21 year old Rose Benta after he accesed her phone and saw whatsapp messages between Benta and another man which alluded to wedding plans. He then sought two men to punish her.
A man kills his wife by slashing her several times on the head, neck an face after he found the wife with another man.

Two people were shot dead and several others injured after chaos erupted during a protest in Ishiara, Embu County. Residents were demonstrating against the poor state of Ishiara Level Four Hospital, citing blocked toilets, lack of an ambulance, and dilapidated infrastructure.

Residents of Ngomeni in Kitui County are living in fear following the fatal shooting of 18-year-old camel herder Osman Hassan Ali, who was killed at a private ranch straddling Kyuso and Mwingi Central sub-counties. The killing has intensified long-standing tensions between farmers and pastoralists along the volatile Kitui–Tana River border.

A gang of robbers broke into a computer shop at Twiga Towers in Nairobi on Saturday night, stealing electronics valued at approximately Sh16 million. The stolen items included computers and mobile phones.CCTV footage captured part of the incident, showing one suspect speaking to the shop’s security guard around 9:00 p.m. before the guard was allegedly drugged and dragged away, leaving him unconscious. It is suspected that the robbers used drugs to incapacitate the guards before carrying out the theft.

Kirinyaga trader Peninah Wambui was strangled to death in her house and her hands burnt.Evidence shows that the perp did not break into the house his access and exit is still a mystery nothing was stolen from the house thus signifying that the intent of the attacker was to end wambui's life.

Susan Achieng was lured by her partner in the name of reconciliation before carrying out the planned brutal assault on her. The intervention of a  neighbour made the attacker flee but he was later arrested. Susan succumbed to her injuries.

A 54-year-old male teacher from Erua Primary School in Narok North was killed after a long-running land dispute with his neighbour. The conflict, which had lasted over 10 years, escalated into violence following an altercation.

A tragic incident occurred in Muthara, Meru County, where a 32-year-old man allegedly killed his two young children—an 8-year-old boy and a 3-year-old girl—by poisoning them and physically assaulting them while they were alone at home.Preliminary accounts from family members suggest that David Mwenda had been experiencing significent stress,particulary after a leg injury that impacted his ability to earn a living as a boda boda ridar.

Lucky Okoth Okoth, had been arrested by Directorate of Criminal Investigations detectives and was being held as investigations continued. The alleged abduction escalated into a ransom case after the suspect reportedly contacted the victim’s family demanding Sh200,000 and threatening harm.

A Nairobi court has issued arrest warrants against two businessmen, Abdisalan Adan Hussein and John Kigomo Mwaura, over a land fraud case involving a prime Westlands property valued at Sh150 million. The accused are alleged to have defrauded the daughters of a deceased businessman.

Residents of Mnagoni and Mapotea group ranches in Ganze Sub-County, Kilifi County, have raised alarm over the alleged illegal sale of community land by certain ranch officials.The situation has led to widespread anger among local residents, leaders, and government officials, with allegations including fraud, abuse of office, and attempts to dispossess the community of ancestral land.

Residents of Ratia Village in Ol Moran, Laikipia County, staged protests following the alleged illegal seizure of their land by private developers. Despite holding legitimate title deeds, the residents claim they were forcibly evicted from their homes.The eviction reportedly took place on a Thursday night, involving individuals accompanied by an armoured vehicle, suggesting intimidation and use of force.

A 45-year-old man, Shimenga, allegedly attacked his three children in Mukoyani Village, Kakamega County, after reportedly becoming emotionally distressed when his estranged wife failed to return home. One child died from severe injuries, while two others were seriously injured and hospitalized. Villagers restrained the suspect before police arrived. Authorities confirmed investigations are ongoing to establish the exact circumstances of the attack.

In Ramula, Siaya County, a dispute over Shanta Gold’s mining operations has escalated into a violent standoff between residents and state authorities. Following the arrest of alleged protest leader Silas Asitiba, the DCI has labeled the unrest as criminal incitement. Conversely, residents and rights groups like Haki Madini Kenya claim the state is using "excessive force" and intimidation to push through opaque land acquisitions without community consent. The conflict remains a clash between official narratives of law enforcement and local claims of human rights violations.
