CocaCola is facing a trademark dispute in Kenya after comedian Inspekta Mwala accused the company and influencer Jacky Vike of infringing on his brand. The issue stems from CocaCola's use of the phrase Ka-Mwala in its "Kachingching na Coke" campaign, which Mwala said caused public confusion and misled fans into thinking he was involved. He has filed suit seeking injuctions, damages and disclosure of profits.

Mercy Awuor, a 34-year-old woman and small business owner in Nyalenda, Kisumu County, was attacked on a Friday evening while walking home from her eatery. Two individuals on a motorbike approached her and, as they passed, the passenger threw a liquid substance on her. Initially believed to be water, it quickly became evident that it was acid when her skin began to burn and her clothing started to disintegrate.
Aden Mohamed Hassan was allegedly killed at Modika in the outskirts of town while responding to a distress call from a friend. Reason for the shoooting is yet to be confirmed.

Lawyer Tom Ouya Imbukwa died after being assaulted at his residence in Harambee Sacco Estate, Donholm, Nairobi. He was found with serious injuries and taken to Kenyatta National Hospital, where he later died in the ICU.

An activist, Francis Awino Onyango, was charged in a Nairobi court with attempting to extort Sh1.7 million from KWS Director-General Prof. Erastus Kanga. The prosecution alleges that Onyango threatened to file a petition seeking Kanga’s removal from office over alleged constitutional violations unless he was paid the money.

The body of a 33 yr old woman who was a hotel worker was found lying in a pool of blood by th roadside by residents heading to work early morning. It is believed she was attacked at around 5am as she was headed to work, none of her belongings were missing.

Asha Wanyonyi aged 26 was sentenced to three years in prison after pleading guilty to stealing a child belonging to Mispher Chepkenol.She  stated that she did the action out of jealousy and vengeance because Chepkenol allegedly had a romantic relationship with  Asha's husband .The incident occurred in Soweto/Kiwerera,where the child was left under the care of the grandmother

Bonventure Aradi, owner of Golden Key Travel Consultants engaged Brian Obare who posed as a Canadian consular to produce travel documents for clients. The documents were fake and most clients were left stranded at the airport while others were arrested. the company lost 51 million KSH.

Fourteen years old Peter Edung was murdered by his fellow teenager Lance using his father's gun. Peter had gone to visit his father who works at the ranch owned by Ivans Tomlinson,Lance's father. The two teenagers are said to have been friends. The police are looking into the cause of the murder.

A group of about 40 bandits killed 7 people in Kwa Kamari,Tseikuru in Kitui county before disappearing into Mwingi North National Reserve which connects to Kora National Park. According to Muasya, a local, it was a retariatory attack after some camel herders had been killed in the area for killing a farmer. Investigations are underway.

A 22 year old Consolata Githinji dies after falling from sixth floor of an apartment in Kileleshwa. The police suspects it to be murder as there had been a spat between her and her lover whom she met on a popular dating website.

Mombasa County, particularly Likoni, is facing growing concern over a series of unresolved murders, many involving women and suspected gender-based violence. The most recent case involves 21-year-old Fidelis Chepchumba, whose decomposing body was discovered in her boyfriend’s house in the Maka area.A post-mortem revealed she had been strangled with bare hands, and her body showed visible facial and neck injuries.

Specific Area: Football Kenya Federation Goal Project Offices
Case Summary: Officers from the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) conducted a raid at the Football Kenya Federation (FKF) offices in Nairobi as part of an ongoing investigation into an insurance fraud scandal tied to preparations for the African Nations Championship (CHAN) 2024.The investigation centres on the alleged mismanagement of approximately USD 4.2 million (KSh 42 million) in insurance funds.
A 14 yr old boy was hacked to death by suspected camel herders. His death lead to protests by resisdents leading blocking of roads thus creating tension in the area.
Tony Odhiambo Lwal is under investigation over the death of Consolata Githinji, a 22-year-old university student who died after falling from the sixth floor of an apartment in Kileleshwa, Nairobi.

Mike Sonko and three co-accused persons were ordered by the Anti-Corruption Court to answer charges in a KSh14 million corruption and graft case linked to an irregular tender for heavy road equipment awarded by Nairobi County in 2018.The case is significant as it highlights misuse of public office and manipulation of county procurement system,the public funds being the primary concern.

Three suspects allegedly vandalized and broke into an official vehicle linked to PS Jane Imbunya while it was parked outside a guest house in Kisumu. Using a blunt object, they smashed the rear window and stole a camera worth Sh400,000 before fleeing. CCTV footage captured parts of the incident, and police investigations are ongoing.

Kamau Mungai Gathage, a chef at Parliament, was fatally stabbed on April 28 at his residence in Ongata Rongai. Following a reported confrontation, Mungai’s girlfriend, who had moved in three weeks prior, allegedly left the house and later returned to alert security that he was injured. Found bleeding profusely by neighbors, Mungai was pronounced dead on arrival at Kenyatta National Hospital. The girlfriend is currently detained as the primary suspect while detectives investigate the motive behind the attack.\

DCI Inspector Daniel Macharia Mburu was arraigned at the Makadara Law courts following the death of his wife, Florence Nyagah. The victim's body was discovered on March 1, 2026, at their home on Lumumba Drive with multiple stab wounds. Macharia surrendered himself to authorities at Naivasha Police Station after his pictures circulated online.

The EACC has presented digital records that captures a chain of communication between Raphael Tuju and a chain of intermediaries who claimed they could influence the outcome of his case before Justice Mongare. The three who claimed to be acting on her behalf solicited bribes on several occassions one of which Mr Tuju liased with EACC detectitives and two suspects sere arrested havink received Sh 1 million treated money.
A PCEA preacher was brutally murdered at his home which was inside the church compound. It is suspected that he was killed for always standing with the truth.

A 7 year old was abducted, raped and brutally murdered. The police report indicate that the deceased had visible injuries on the right side of her face, bruises on her hands and had signs of being sexually assaulted.

Specific Area: Jilore Senior School,Dr Aggrey Boys National School,St Mary's Boys High School and Mapi Comprehensive Junior day
Case Summary: A wave of student unrest swept across parts of Kenya’s Coast region, leading to the destruction of four schools in Kilifi, Kwale, and Taita Taveta counties. The incidents mainly involved arson attacks on dormitories and school facilities, causing extensive property damage but no reported fatalities.

Police in Nairobi are investigating the murder of a 52 year old widow, whose body was discovered in her house located in Mukuru Kwa Njenga slums. Concern arose when neighbours noticed a strong smell coming from the house, prompting investigation.The primary suspect is the victim’s son, a young adult in his mid‑twenties, who had reportedly been seen with the victim shortly before the incident and later observed with unusually large amounts of money.

Authorities in Homa Bay County are investigating the murder of a 35-year-old fisherman, Fredrick Oduol, who died following a violent dispute over fishing grounds at Mikuyu Beach in Suba South.The incident occurred during a fishing expedition when two groups of fishermen clashed after one group accused the other of operating in an area not allocated to them. The confrontation escalated into a physical fight, during which the victim was struck with a paddle, sustaining serious injuries.

A major land dispute in the Marurui area of Nairobi has resulted in the demolition of about 80 homes, leaving over 100 families homeless. The affected residents had purchased subdivided plots from a private firm, which issued them with what they believed were legitimate title deeds.

Specific Area: Near Mbakuri,close to Iriani primary school
Case Summary: The report describes a disturbing incident in Tharaka Nithi County involving the killing of a young girl under brutal circumstances.A three year old child named Shirley Gatum, had gone missing on May 4, 2026, while heading to a relative’s home near Iriani Primary School. The child’s body was discovered a day later near Mbakuri.Medical and investigative reports indicate that the victim was strangled and dismembered, highlighting the extreme violence involved.

Residents and motorists using the Kimbo–Matangi–Junction Road complained about worsening road conditions and alleged corruption by police officers stationed along the route. According to reports, the officers openly collected Sh50 bribes from tuktuk drivers and other motorists, operating what locals described as an illegal “toll station

Kristabel Anyango, a 28-year-old student, was found dead after visiting her boyfriend in Syokimau in an attempt to reconcile their troubled relationship. Family members became concerned after days of unanswered calls and cryptic text messages sent from her phone. Her boyfriend later informed the family that she had collapsed and was in hospital, but provided few details. Police later informed the family that Kristabel had died. A postmortem examination revealed she died from blunt force trauma, with defensive injuries on her hands suggesting she tried to protect herself during the attack. The family has raised concerns about the handling of the case by Syokimau Police Station, and the Directorate of Criminal Investigations has since taken over the investigation.

Eleven suspects connected to the management of NG-CDF funds in Eldama Ravine were arraigned in a Nakuru court over the alleged loss of more than Sh85 million intended for community development projects between the 2018/2019 and 2020/2021 financial years. The accused, including NG-CDF committee members and County Treasury officials, face charges related to abuse of office, conspiracy to commit economic crimes, and fraudulent acquisition of public property. Prosecutors allege the suspects jointly conspired to illegally acquire and misuse funds allocated for development projects in the constituency.

An elderly man was found dead in a lodging room in Kiminini after reportedly checking in with a woman on Thursday. Hotel workers became suspicious when the man failed to respond after the woman had left the room and alerted the hotel owner. Police found the man dead, with his ATM and identification cards still intact, leaving uncertainty over whether theft had occurred. Authorities stated they would await postmortem results to determine the cause of death as investigations continue.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba warned school principals and administrators against imposing illegal levies and engaging in financial mismanagement, citing the Alliance Girls High School case as an example. The government announced plans for disciplinary and legal action against implicated school heads. Concerns were raised over excessive and questionable expenditures despite schools facing reduced capitation funding. The article highlights growing scrutiny of how public school funds are managed and the financial burden placed on parents.

Residents of the tea-growing region in Kigumo Constituency, Murang’a, have taken to patrolling their own neighborhoods at night following a surge in livestock theft. Over the last three weeks, at least ten cows and goats have been stolen from Kinyona, prompting community leaders like Simon Maina to organize local security watches. During a recent patrol in Muthiria and Gikoe villages, residents intercepted a pickup truck transporting avocados after hours. This incident highlights a growing link between illegal avocado trading and livestock theft, leading local security authorities to officially ban the harvesting of avocados between 6:00 PM and 6:00 AM to curb criminal activity.

Six people were killed and three critically injured when four armed men ambushed a minibus at Umar Jilo in Mandera. The vehicle was transporting 15 passengers, including community elders, to a family event in Arabia town. While most survivors have been traced, one passenger remains missing. A multi-agency security team is currently pursuing the attackers, who are suspected militants, amid a recent surge of violence in the region.

The EACC is the process of recovering 20.17 acres of land in Karen that was allocated to KBC but was fraudulently subdivided by Sammy Mwaita during his tenure as land commissioner and allocated it to development accompanies

A fierce multi-billion-shilling shadow battle is unfolding over the fraudulent acquisition of a vast 9,000-acre piece of land belonging to the state-owned Miwani Sugar Company. Internal government documents and investigation reports reveal that a powerful cartel of lawyers, land registrars, and private sector operatives successfully orchestrated a highly sophisticated scheme to secularize and transfer the public asset into private hands. The fraud relied on a dormant 1993 court case that was illegally resurrected decades later using forged signatures of a deceased deputy registrar to clear the path for a questionable public auction, where a company called Crossley Holdings Limited "purchased" the land for Sh352 million. Despite a highly controversial 2018 lower court ruling that acquitted the key suspects, the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) has appealed to the High Court, as ongoing state investigations reveal that the land ownership documents were completely fabricated, no court fees were ever paid, and the entire transaction was engineered to strip the state of one of Kenya's largest public land assets.
Four gang members attacked the Church's security guard Bernand Nyamwaka and torturing him for hours.The guard survived despite serious injuries and is now under protection as a key witness.

Alice's  body was found last Saturday  in  a forest in Barkowino by women who had gone to fetch firewood. Her boyfriend is the current suspect as he was the one who had contact with the Alice. Alice had been  missing for a while before her body was discovered in the forest.

Police in Nairobi are investigating a coordinated car-part theft syndicate after a United Nations vehicle was targeted in Parklands. The suspects forcefully removed the car’s front grille while the driver was inside, despite resistance. Dashboard camera footage captured the incident and enabled police to identify three suspects.Two key suspects, James Omuya and John Owiti, were arrested shortly afterward, along with another accomplice.

Bonface ondara a teacher in Njoro boys highschool reported that on May 6 he was attacked by the principal at the reception at around 11am following a disagreementof which the principal John Githaiga did not update his Teacher management information management details amid him joining the school and transferring his previous details from his previous school to Njoro boys.

Advocate Reuben is alledged to have filed lawsuits on behalf of 5 groups of cooperative societies seeking to stop the lenders annual general meeting yet the societies claim they did not instruct any lawyer to institute the proceedings on their behalf, thus this is seen as impersonation with intent to extort the bank

A 15-year-old girl was acquitted of manslaughter charges for the death of her infant, which she allegedly threw into a pit latrine after birth, causing suffocation. The girl claimed she became pregnant after being defiled by a priest, and killed the baby when he refused to take responsibility.

Five University of Nairobi students—Beres Muthomi, Trace Phanice Auma, Patience Gitau, Kenneth Juma, and Samuel Jomanga—were charged at the Milimani Law Courts with offensive conduct likely to cause a breach of peace. The prosecution alleged that on May 11, 2026, during the Africa Forward Summit at the University of Nairobi, they threw stones and shouted, disrupting proceedings attended by Kenyan President William Ruto and French President Emmanuel Macron.

Police in Kayole arrested four suspects believed to be involved in a mobile phone-snatching gang targeting residents in the area. The May 12 operation in the Saika area along Kangundo Road led to the recovery of 62 mobile phones, three motorcycles, a television set, and other stolen household items. Officers also recovered a Falcon pistol and 16 rounds of ammunition.

Specific Area: Forest View area along Musikoma–Bumula Road
Case Summary: A public health officer, Pascal Wakafura, was killed in the Forest View area along the Musikoma–Bumula Road in Bungoma County on the evening of May 11, 2026. Neighbours later discovered his body lying in a pool of blood with severe injuries.

Motive: To secure employment at the university
Case Summary: A former employee of Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology was arraigned before the Kakamega Anti-Corruption Court for allegedly forging academic certificates to obtain employment at the institution.

A 15-year-old girl was acquitted of manslaughter charges for the death of her infant, which she allegedly threw into a pit latrine after birth, causing suffocation. The girl claimed she became pregnant after being defiled by a priest, and killed the baby when he refused to take responsibility.
A 20-year-old man identified as Shukran Mwarambai was lynched by an angry mob in Baricho village, Magarini Sub-County in Kilifi County after being accused of stealing two cows.

Motive: Enforce police recruitment standards and discipline.
Case Summary: The dismissal of 54police recruits from training colleges, especially in Kiganjo, exposing broader concerns about flaws within Kenya’s police recruitment system. Authorities defended the removals as part of enforcing discipline and professional standards, citing pregnancy, forged documents, criminal records, and medical conditions among reasons for dismissal.

authorities have launched investigations into millions of shillings allegedly missing from FKF accounts. The probe follows concerns over suspected financial irregularities, poor accounting practices, and unaccounted sponsorship funds within the federation. Former FKF officials, including Nick Mwendwa, are mentioned in connection with earlier investigations by the DCI into alleged financial misconduct. The article highlights ongoing scrutiny over how football revenues and sponsorship money were managed and whether funds were illegally diverted or misused.

Wildlife Principal Secretary Silvia Museiya faced criticism after lawmakers questioned the diversion of Sh300 million from a compensation fund meant for victims of wildlife attacks to a digital consultancy project. Members of the National Assembly Committee on Tourism and Wildlife demanded explanations over the expenditure, arguing that many victims and affected families were still waiting for compensation. State department officials defended the spending, saying the funds supported a pilot digitisation programme for processing compensation claims. However, MPs expressed concern about transparency, value for money, and the continued suffering of victims awaiting justice and financial support.

Four students from Magereza Academy in Naivasha were arrested after a dormitory fire destroyed school property worth thousands of shillings and forced the indefinite closure of the institution. The blaze occurred while students were attending evening classes, and some students sustained minor injuries while attempting to rescue their belongings before firefighters contained the fire. CCTV footage allegedly placed the four students at the scene, leading to their arrest by police investigators.

Police in Migori have apprehended a 32-year-old man suspected of being behind a string of violent robberies in the region. According to Suna East Sub-County Police Commander Harriet Hailey, the suspect—who claims to be a businessman—had been under police surveillance for nearly two months prior to his arrest at the Isebania border. During the operation, authorities discovered a Taurus revolver and ten rounds of ammunition hidden inside his vehicle near the gear shift. The suspect is currently being held at the Migori Police Station pending ballistic testing of the weapon and is expected to face charges in court on Monday.

Specific Area: The Nairobi Hospital, Pumwani Maternity Hospital, Nairobi Women’s Hospital, Elgon View Hospital and Mater Misericordiae Hospital.
Case Summary: The article examines the ongoing crisis of hospitals illegally detaining patients and deceased bodies due to unsettled medical bills, a practice widely condemned by the Kenyan judiciary as a violation of human rights. Despite a decade of clear court precedents stating that hospitals have no legal authority to act as "holding cells," many facilities continue to ignore these rulings to secure payment. The report highlights several harrowing cases, such as mothers forced to sleep on floors and heart patients held for months after being cleared for discharge, which leads to the accumulation of even higher "detention fees." While judges have ordered structural changes and the Ministry of Health to intervene, health advocates argue that the lack of enforcement mechanisms and a failing insurance system leave vulnerable Kenyans trapped between medical necessity and illegal imprisonment.
Detectives are investigating the alleged abduction of Fortune Muthina who was linked to a caller ID spoofing fraud syndicate and had an ongoing case at the Kahawa law courts.
Goons stormed CocaCola depot in Kitengela shortly after midday and vandalised and looted from the premises during the fuel hike protests.
Motorists, commuters and pedestrians along southern bypass were extorted by armed goons who blocked the road with trailers and bonfires demanding cash from drivers and harassing pedetrians.

Racheal Wandeto was alledgly attacked by three people on her way home with an unknown liquid .She suffered severe burns from the liquid and was rushed to KNH for treatment but she succumbed to her injuries on Monday. The reason for the attack is yet to be determined.

Across Nairobi and other parts of the country kenyans conducted protests against the rise of fuel prices and some were caught up in the battle between the police and the protesters and were shot to death even though they were not armed.

Valery Amondi was injured after being shot in the torso and is currently recovering in hospital. According to the victim’s statement, Valery Amondi was not involved in the protests that were taking place and was instead on the way to work, maintaining distance from the demonstrators at the time the shooting occurred.

During demonstrations in Wote, Makueni County, violent clashes broke out between a large group of youths and police officers. The confrontation escalated into physical attacks on law enforcement, resulting in two police officers sustaining injuries and being hospitalised.Amid the chaos caused by tear gas deployment and crowd dispersal, a group of youths reportedly surrounded police officers and stole a firearm from one officer before fleeing.

A 20-year-old individual identified as Prudence Imali was shot and killed in Marurui, a location within Nairobi. The body of Prudence Imali was transferred to the Kenyatta National Hospital mortuary following the incident.
A total of nine trucks were burned,while three supermarkets were looted and subsequently set on fire during protest unrest.The scale of property destruction had a severe impact on local businesses.

The incident occurred during nationwide protests against rising fuel prices, which led to unrest across several Kenyan counties. In Kakamega, tensions escalated when police attempted to disperse demonstrators moving from the central business district toward Maraba.During the confrontation, police reportedly opened fire on protesters. One of the victims, Derrick Machanja, a student at Sigalagala National Polytechnic, was shot and later died from head injuries. Reports indicate that he collapsed after being shot while protests were being dispersed.

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud was attacked by a group of youths in Kangemi and later hospitalised. The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) intended to charge several suspects with serious offences including assault, arson, and robbery with violence.

A 32-year-old boda boda rider, George Kariuki, was fatally shot during protests linked to rising fuel prices and a matatu strike. The incident occurred near a shopping centre in the Dandora/Dagoretti area, only a few metres from his residence in an informal settlement.
A grade 8 pupil of Masana Secondary School was found Dead after going missing on Monday evening after school.

A grade 6 pupil Mercy Nyambura was found dead in a maize plantation at lare, Njoro sub county. Allegedly defilled, tortoured and killed. Her body bore multiple injuries, bruises on the neck and severe injuries on the face.
Dishen  Angoya (OCS Nairobi central police station) was arrested after abuse of office by releasing 64 suspect arrested over public order offence.

A lobby group known as the Centre for Litigation Trust filed a petition in the High Court seeking orders compelling Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen and Inspector General Douglas Kanja to immediately reinstate the security detail assigned to Siaya Governor James Orengo. According to court filings and Orengo’s protest letter, his personal and residential security officers were abruptly withdrawn on May 19, 2026, without prior notice, explanation, or replacement officers being assigned.

Residents of Isiolo County were shocked after authorities and family members discovered suspected human remains along with clothes and shoes believed to belong to missing businessman George Gitonga. Gitonga had disappeared on the night of May 1 at around 9 pm. Police confirmed the discovery during an active search operation. Investigators stated that the recovered clothing and shoes appear to match what the trader was wearing before he vanished. The case remains under investigation, with no suspects or motive identified so far.

Specific Area: Chemalal Mixed Day and Boarding Secondary School
Case Summary: A 17-year-old Form Three student from Chemalal Mixed Day and Boarding Secondary School in Bomet County was seriously injured after allegedly being stabbed by her 23-year-old classmate during a Christian Union session. Police say the attack may have been linked to a suspected love triangle and a secret relationship between the two students. The suspect reportedly used a knife to stab the girl in the chest and left arm before members of the public responded to her screams and attacked him. He was later rescued and handed over to the police as investigations continue.

Motive: Violence connected to fuel-related demonstrations and unrest
Case Summary: A 17-year-old boy identified as Harrison Karanja died after being shot in the head during fuel-related protests in Naivasha. The unrest resulted in widespread destruction, including vandalism of supermarkets and the burning of trucks. Authorities reported that at least 11 people suffered gunshot injuries while more than 100 suspects were arrested over the chaos and looting. Another student was reportedly injured by a stray bullet during the demonstrations. The incident raised the death toll from the protests to three as investigations and arrests continued.

The case involves police officer Philip Edasi and his accomplices, Mahat Abdullahi and Earnest Odongo, who were charged with robbery with violence after using a fake highway checkpoint to rob businesswoman Suad Zaid Abdi of over Sh14.1 million in cash and electronics.

Specific Area: Kariobangi area, backsreets, garages, slum areas, industrial zones in Nairobi
Case Summary: An Organized criminal syndicate in Nairobi is involved in stealing vehicles, dismantling them and selling the parts through illegal spare-parts networks involving gangs, mechanics, dealers and cartels for financial gain.

Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka raised concerns over the existence of about 1,000 alleged ghost workers within the county government payroll. He warned county officials accused of facilitating the fraudulent recruitment scheme that stern disciplinary and legal action would be taken. Lusaka announced that a forensic audit would be conducted to identify how the ghost workers contributed to the county’s growing wage bill. Some employees had already been suspended pending investigations.

Motive: Dispute that escalated into a physical confrontation
Case Summary: A man identified as Stephen Mbugua Mwangi was arrested in Limuru, Kiambu County, for allegedly stabbing his neighbour, George Kimani, after a dispute in the Ngarariga area escalated into a physical fight. Kimani was rushed to Limuru Nursing Home by good Samaritans but died from his injuries upon arrival. Police obtained 21 days to detain the suspect as investigations continue. Following the incident, angry residents allegedly attempted to burn down the suspect’s house, but police intervened and prevented the attack.

The death of 22-year-old university student Brian Njuguna Ndungu while in police custody. His family says he was arrested over alleged theft accusations but later died under unclear circumstances. Police reportedly claimed Brian died by suicide after hanging himself using a shoelace, but the family strongly disputes this explanation. Relatives who viewed the body reported visible injuries, blood stains, and swelling, raising suspicions of torture or assault while in detention. The family is demanding justice and an independent investigation into the events leading to his death.
A sophisticated student loan and financial aid fraud involving identity theft has been linked to operators in Nairobi. The US government has lost Sh 12 billion through the fraud.

Specific Area: Wayside Junction along Nyerere Road Kisumu
Case Summary: A 39 year old Were was beaten to death at Wayside Junction in Kisumu County. The Police are still investigating the matter.
A former soldier, David Muigei, discovered that he had been falsely declared dead and issued with a death certificate while still alive, raising allegations of forgery and fraud.

Specific Area: Free Area Estate(near gate of their home) Nakuru
Case Summary: During a nationwide protest over fuel prices in Nakuru County, 13-year-old Grade Seven pupil Joseph Njuguna was shot in the jaw by anti-riot police using live bullets while playing near his home's gate in the Free Area estate. He narrowly survived after undergoing surgery at Nakuru Level V Hospital to remove the bullet, leaving his family with heavy medical bills and severe psychological trauma. While his mother reported the matter to the Mwariki Police Station and the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), local human rights defenders and neighbors have strongly condemned the police's use of excessive, lethal force within residential areas.

Specific Area: Minjila junction along the Lamu-Witu -Garsen road
Motive: Demand enforcement of high court ruling
Case Summary: Residents and human rights activists in Lamu County protested against the continued enforcement of a night travel curfew (6pm–7am) that has been in place since 2017. The protests followed a High Court ruling issued in Garsen suspending the curfew, pending the determination of a legal petition challenging its legality.

Motive: Dispute over illegal high rise development
Case Summary: The two chiefs were attacked  during a meeting in Kileleshwa over dispute of high-rise developments in Kileleshwa. Mr. Alai accussed the administrators of colluding with developers to manipulate public participation process to facilitate illegal construction projects.

A 17-year-old Form Four student in Nakuru County was allegedly attacked with acid by a 24-year-old man after she rejected his romantic advances. The incident occurred early in the morning while she was walking to school.

Motive: Enforcement of CBD decongestion and relocation policy
Case Summary: A committee of the Nairobi County Assembly criticised the Nairobi City County Government over the eviction of book vendors from Nairobi CBD, saying enforcement officers violated traders’ constitutional rights through harassment, confiscation of goods and discriminatory crackdowns.

A political dispute emerged in Kajiado County after journalist Jonathan Teikan was ordered by court to pay Sh16 million to Katoo Ole Metito in a defamation case. The case arose from an online story alleging Mr Metito’s involvement in irregular land acquisition at Rombo Group Ranch.

Specific Area: Cross-border routes linking Kenya, Uganda, and areas towards Ethiopia
Case Summary: The growing threat posed by organized cross-border motorcycle theft syndicates operating across Kenya and neighboring countries. In one incident, Noah Simiyu was attacked by two men and a woman armed with a machete in Bungoma County as they attempted to steal his motorcycle, while in another case thieves stole John Bitok's motorcycle from Nandi Hills before it was recovered in Kisumu. Investigators say these crimes are increasingly carried out by coordinated criminal networks that steal motorcycles, disable tracking systems, alter identification details, and smuggle the bikes through unofficial border routes into neighboring countries where they are resold, dismantled, or re-registered. Authorities in Kenya and Uganda have responded by enhancing cross-border cooperation and intelligence sharing to combat the growing criminal enterprise, which threatens the livelihoods of thousands of boda boda operators who depend on motorcycles as their primary source of income.

Four students—three Form Four girls and one Form Three girl—were arrested in connection with a dormitory fire at St Paul’s Githakwa Secondary School in Nyeri County. The fire, which broke out in the Blessed Sister Irene Nyaatha Dormitory on the night of May 26, destroyed property belonging to 25 students but caused no fatalities or serious injuries after a student spotted the blaze and raised the alarm, allowing all occupants to evacuate safely. Preliminary investigations suggest the fire was premeditated and may have been motivated by fear of upcoming end-of-term examinations, influence from recent school unrest, and tensions arising from a dispute over missing school uniforms. Police recovered an empty matchbox and a container suspected to have held an inflammable substance, and investigations into the incident are ongoing.

A 17-year-old boy died after allegedly being assaulted by security guards at a multinational tea estate in Konoin, Bomet County. According to Area Police Commander Muhammed Godana, the guards reportedly beat the teenager and left him unconscious. Good Samaritans rushed him to Kaptebengwet Dispensary before he was transferred to Longisa County Referral Hospital for specialized treatment. Although he initially presented with bruises on his face and hands, medical reports indicated that he ultimately died from internal bleeding. Police investigations into the incident are ongoing.

A patient named Brian Simiyu died at Tophill Hospital in Eldoret following a botched stomach surgery performed on May 17, 2026, by an unlicensed doctor at Samor Clinic in Kitale. According to the victim's sister, Lydia Sizie, the operation was conducted under horrific conditions in a dirty room lacking basic surgical equipment, where the fake doctor even used a standard cloth instead of cotton wool to wipe blood. After the family paid Sh32,000 for the procedure, Simiyu's condition rapidly deteriorated at home, suffering from an intestinal infection and kidney failure that led to his death on May 28. The tragedy sparked local protests demanding a crackdown on illegal clinics, prompting the Surgical Society of Kenya to condemn the incident and county authorities to arrest the suspect and shut down the unlicensed facility.

Specific Area: Utumishi Girls Senior School in Gilgil
Case Summary: Homicide detectives have narrowed down their investigation to eight Form Three female students implicated in a horrific arson attack at Utumishi Girls Senior School that killed 16 students and injured 79 others. The fire, which broke out in the middle of the night at the Meline Waithera Block B dormitory, was reportedly started by disgruntled students protesting administrative high-handedness. Investigators successfully isolated the eight suspects out of an initial group of 30 after reviewing CCTV footage, securing confessions from guilt-ridden participants, and analyzing witness accounts from fellow students. Beyond the students facing criminal charges, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba revealed that the tragic outcome was severely compounded by safety violations—including a congested floor plan and a locked exit door—resulting in immediate disciplinary action against the school principal and two teachers who ignored advance warnings of the plot.
There has been a surge in defilement and GBV in Bomet. This is according to Bomet East Sub-County police commander Michael Singa.
More than 3000 residents of Samburet joined by members of the Ogiek community pulled the fence of Browns Tea Company siting alleged land grabbing.

30 Year old Kenneth Toroitich vanishes following a series of phone calls only for his body to be found near Lake Elementaita a week later with serious injuries.A post-mortem examination revealed that Kenneth died from severe head injuries and strangulation. The body also showed signs of violence, including neck injuries and burns suspected to have been caused by a corrosive substance. Detectives are investigating the circumstances surrounding his disappearance and murder, while family members and the Baringo community are demanding justice and the arrest of those responsible.

Specific Area: Kileleshwa, Lavington, Kilimani, Eastleigh, South C and Minnesota USA
Case Summary: Muhammad Abdulqadir Omar, a suspect in a massive US$90 million (Sh11.7 billion) Minnesota healthcare fraud scheme, was arrested by the FBI after months on the run. Omar and his business partner, Ibrahim Bashir Abdi, allegedly used two home healthcare companies to fraudulently bill Minnesota's Medicaid programme by forging client signatures and claiming payments for services that were never rendered or were billed for hospitalized or deceased clients. The illicit proceeds were subsequently wired to Kenya to purchase lucrative real estate investments in high-end Nairobi neighbourhoods like Kileleshwa and Lavington. During a raid on his Minnesota apartment, Omar attempted a dramatic escape by jumping from a fourth-floor balcony, breaking his leg before being captured hours later. Following his arrest, discussions intensified between the FBI and Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) to strengthen international cooperation on combating transnational financial fraud, cybercrime, and money laundering.

The case involved the fraudelent diversion of ksh 51.69 million from Kilifi county procurement fraud.The direct victim was Kilifi County and its residents,while 10 individuals and companies were convicted

Motive: Enforcement against illegal grazing on ADC land
Case Summary: A series of alleged extra-judicial killings linked to security operations at Agricultural Development Corporation (ADC) farms in Trans Nzoia County has raised serious concerns among residents. The situation reflects long-standing tensions over land ownership, illegal grazing, and security enforcement in the region.The most recent incident involved the fatal shooting of a 40-year-old Kitale resident, Dennis Kwemoi, during a police operation. According to a police report, six Kenya Police Reserve (KPR) officers were on patrol in the Arran area when they intercepted approximately 20 cows allegedly grazing illegally on a sugarcane plantation.

A tragic domestic incident occurred in Kong’onge Village in Rachuonyo West, Homabay County, where a 30-year-old parent killed two young children before taking own life. Reports indicate that the incident was linked to alleged fears of a marital dispute involving the possibility of a co-wife

Specific Area: Bomani ground in Mumias West Constituency
Case Summary: The report highlights violent clashes that erupted in Mumias West Constituency in Kakamega County following Madaraka Day celebrations at Bomani Grounds. The unrest occurred after an event attended by political leaders, including Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa.Groups of youths engaged in confrontations with police, leading to widespread disorder. The clashes escalated into running battles, with demonstrators erecting roadblocks, lighting bonfires, and blocking major roads such as the Kakamega–Mumias and Kakamega–Musanda highways. This disruption significantly affected transport and local economic activities.

Motive: Dispute over changes in House leadership
Case Summary: The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has officially summoned 35 Members of the Narok County Assembly to record statements following a violent brawl that erupted inside the assembly chambers on May 19. In a letter sent by EACC Deputy Director David Kiboro to County Assembly Clerk Joseph Lengeny, the legislators were ordered to appear before investigators at the Integrity Centre in Nairobi between June 9 and June 22. The physical confrontation, which disrupted assembly proceedings and shocked local residents, stemmed from deep political divisions regarding changes in House leadership and allegations that the County Executive was interfering with Assembly committee structures. The EACC is investigating the incident as a matter of serious unethical conduct, highlighting growing political tensions in the region ahead of the 2027 polls.

Two protesters were killed on Monday in Nanyuki, during proetests over planned US Ebola quarantine facility at the Laikipia Air Base. It is yet to be determined who made the shot either the millitary or the police.

Detectives raided a Nairobi County official's Syokimau home and recovered about KSh 63 million in cash and assets suspected to be inconsistent with his known income, as part of an anti-corruption investigation.

Ten students from Alliance High School were arrested after a fire gutted a school store containing old mattresses. The incident reportedly began as student misconduct and classroom disturbances before escalating into arson, with CCTV evidence allegedly capturing two boys involved in setting the fire. The school administration, education officials, and security agencies are investigating the incident, which has raised nationwide concern over increasing school unrest and fire outbreaks.

Witnesses and industry insiders stated that the vehicle had successfully performed the stunt at one roundabout before attempting it again at a second roundabout, where it lost balance and rolled over. Family members of the victims accused authorities of failing to curb dangerous matatu practices and alleged that the driver had been behaving irresponsibly. The incident has reignited public debate about Nairobi's "Nganya" culture and the risks posed by stunt driving in the public transport sector.

Motive: Personal financial enrichment through abuse of authority
Case Summary: The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) raided the Syokimau home of Nairobi County Chief Officer for Urban Planning Patrick Analo Akivaga and recovered approximately KSh 65.3 million in cash, alongside land documents, vehicle records, electronic devices, and Nairobi County approval documents. Investigators are examining allegations of bribery, abuse of office, conflict of interest, and possession of unexplained wealth, suspecting that Mr. Analo may have accumulated assets disproportionate to his known income while serving in influential positions within Nairobi County's planning department. The case has intensified scrutiny of the department's role in development approvals and longstanding complaints about corruption, illegal developments, and questionable planning decisions. Investigations remain ongoing, and no court has yet determined Mr. Analo's guilt.

A fatal shooting at the ADC Olng’atongo Farm in Endebess, Trans Nzoia County, left 40-year-old Dennis Kwemoi dead after an alleged confrontation between Kenya Police Reservists and local residents over cattle grazing on government land. Police claim the victim charged at an officer, prompting the shooting, while critics and human rights groups view the incident as part of a broader pattern of alleged extrajudicial killings by security personnel guarding state-owned land. The incident sparked violent protests, with residents torching sugarcane fields and property worth millions, and has intensified calls for accountability, compensation, and investigations by the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), which is already handling multiple similar cases.

Motive: Intimidating and harming local political rival leaders.
Case Summary: Kisii County is experiencing growing concern over a wave of political violence targeting political leaders and public figures. The latest incident involved Kitutu Ward MCA Wycliffe Siocha, who was attacked near Gusii Stadium while waiting for his vehicle to be serviced. Witnesses reported that a group of approximately 10 assailants, believed to have been trailing him, descended on him and assaulted him with kicks, blows, and sharp objects. Political leaders and residents have expressed concern over increasing acts of violence allegedly carried out by organized groups of political goons. Police have acknowledged the incidents and pledged to investigate and arrest those responsible. The attacks have intensified fears about political intolerance and insecurity in Kisii County.

Police are investigating the death of Eugene Mutuku, a 19-year-old KMTC Yatta student, who died after allegedly falling from a moving matatu along Thika Road. Reports indicate that the student may have been pushed out of the vehicle following a dispute over fare payment.

Police in Homa Bay County arrested a man accused of murdering his brother, Lucas Killion, following a dispute over the ownership of a tree located on a contested land boundary in Wakula North, Suba West. The two brothers had reportedly been involved in a prolonged disagreement over the boundary.According to police, the brothers convened a meeting to resolve the dispute, and the victim was advised by his mother to end the matter peacefully. However, before the meeting concluded, the suspect allegedly left, went to his house, retrieved a panga, and attacked his brother. Lucas Killion died at the scene from the injuries sustained.

Specific Area: Nairobi School, Maranda High School, Lenana School, Kisii School, Alliance High School, Moi Forces Academy Lanet, Loreto High School, Highway Secondary School, Pumwani Secondary School, and Our Lady of Mercy Shauri Moyo Girls Secondary School
Case Summary: The article details a rising wave of unrest and violent protests spreading across Kenya’s previously stable, prestigious national and elite boarding schools, forcing multiple institutions to close indefinitely and send students home. In response to the growing chaos—which has seen classrooms, labs, and CCTV networks destroyed at Lenana School and a captain's room torched at Kisii School—Education Principal Secretary Belio Kipsang issued a stern warning that the government will show zero tolerance, promising that culprits will be identified and criminally prosecuted. While students' immediate triggers ranged from complaints about entertainment choices to the management of festival funds, education stakeholders and religious leaders point to deeper systemic crises. They attribute the breakdown to poor communication, mental health struggles, severe congestion in boarding facilities, and intense academic pressure, prompting some religious leaders to call for the gradual phasing out of the traditional boarding school model entirely.

Motive: Dispute linked to the management of the mosque
Case Summary: Muslim clerics and residents of Lamu county condemned the killing of Khalid Maka inside Faza mosque during prayers. The act is described as violation of the sanctity of places of worship and called for peace and unity.They urged parents,comunity leaders, and securityagencies to work together to prevent violence and promote moral values.

Osman Aweeys, an 18 -year old US citizen was allegedly robbed and fatally Tstabbed by a knife-wielding gang riding on two motorcycles while he visited his family in Garissa. The incident has heightened fears over the rising insecurity and inccreasing cases of violent crime in the county.R esidents and  leaders have urged security agencies to take swift action and bring the perpetrators to justice.

An unannounced evening raid by over ten police officers at Kisumu's Attela Beach resort escalated into chaos after an unknown individual threw a stone at the forces. Police retaliated by firing tear gas into the crowd, and during the ensuing commotion, security guard Undrine Adhiambo Sire was shot in the thigh while attempting to stop an officer from deploying more gas. The heavy-handed operation—which appeared targeting shisha usage as pots were confiscated—resulted in several patron injuries, significant property damage, and severe financial losses from unpaid bills. In response to the violence, resort management filed an official complaint with the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), while local tourism bodies have strongly condemned the raid for threatening the region's waterfront economy.

Motive: To facilitate the escape of the accused crew members and prevent them from being arrested by law enforcement
Case Summary: Two operations managers at Nicco Sacco, Whines Momanyi Mogire and Alex Mwai Kabuthi, have been charged with conspiring to conceal evidence and helping a minibus crew flee from law enforcement after a fatal accident. The charges stem from a June 5 incident where 19-year-old student Eugine Mutuku fell from a moving minibus on the Thika Road service lane and was subsequently run over by the vehicle. Instead of reporting the accident, the managers allegedly chose to hide the minibus and facilitate the escape of the driver and conductor. Mutuku later succumbed to severe injuries at Kenyatta National Hospital after a Good Samaritan notified the police. Appearing before Makadara Principal Magistrate Gilbert Shikwe, the two managers denied the charges and were each granted a Sh1 million bond with no cash bail alternative, with the hearing scheduled for September 15.

Five students from Magereza Academy have been charged in court with arson and malicious damage to property after being accused of planning and carrying out an attack that set part of a dormitory ablaze forcing closure of the school.

Motive: Block set-up of an Ebola isolation unit for the US citizens exposed to Ebola in the DR Congo due to perceived health, safety, and economic risks
Case Summary: Dozens of protesters were arrested in Nanyuki town following day-long, chaotic demonstrations against the establishment of a Sh17 billion, US-funded Ebola quarantine facility at the Laikipia Air Base. Residents engaged in running battles with police, who were forced to call for reinforcements from Kiganjo Police College after a late-night ban on the protests was defied by the public. The 50-bed bio-isolation unit, intended to quarantine US nationals exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has sparked fierce local outrage over a complete lack of public participation and the defiance of a court order halting its construction. Joining the uproar, the Laikipia County Government has backed high court petitions filed by the Katiba Institute and the Law Society of Kenya, accusing President Ruto's administration of completely sidelining them from critical health and safety decisions that have already triggered immediate economic damage, including widespread tourist cancellations for local hotels.

Motive: Building a new state lodge, an airstrip, and a golf course
Case Summary: A wave of public anger has erupted over a controversial directive from President William Ruto’s administration to clear 100 acres of Meru County's pristine Imenti Forest for a new state lodge, golf course, and airstrip. Local communities, conservationists, and the Green Belt Movement have fiercely condemned the project, warning that it threatens a critical elephant migration corridor and an essential water catchment zone. Opponents argue that destroying protected land is unnecessary given that another state lodge is located barely 100 kilometers away in Nyeri. While Meru Governor Eric Mutuma and Forestry Principal Secretary Gitonga Mugambi defend the move as an economic boost for the youth, critics call out the blatant hypocrisy of slicing up a gazetted forest while the national government simultaneously promotes an ambitious campaign to plant 15 billion trees.

Motive: Establish a Sh17 billion, 50-bed bio-isolation unit to quarantine and treat American citizens exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo
Case Summary: Dozens of protesters were arrested in Nanyuki town following day-long, chaotic demonstrations against the establishment of a Sh17 billion, US-funded Ebola quarantine facility at the Laikipia Air Base. Residents engaged in running battles with police, who were forced to call for reinforcements from Kiganjo Police College after a late-night ban on the protests was defied by the public. The 50-bed bio-isolation unit, intended to quarantine US nationals exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has sparked fierce local outrage over a complete lack of public participation and the defiance of a court order halting its construction. Joining the uproar, the Laikipia County Government has backed high court petitions filed by the Katiba Institute and the Law Society of Kenya, accusing President Ruto's administration of completely sidelining them from critical health and safety decisions that have already triggered immediate economic damage, including widespread tourist cancellations for local hotels.

Three students from Kisumu Boys High School were arrested and charged with attempted arson.Their bond was denied because the court determined the applicants faced immediate threat to life if released.The court deemed it necesarry for a pre-bail report to be prepared before a determination in bond is made.

The Auditor-General, Nancy Gathungu, found that eight county governments—Bomet County, Garissa County, Isiolo County, Samburu County, Nyeri County, Migori County, Nyamira County and Embu County—continued paying salaries and allowances to employees who had already reached the mandatory retirement age.

Former Tigania East Member of Parliament Joseph Kinyua Mwirabua (David Kabebea) was detained after being charged with 24 counts of obtaining money by false pretences from land buyers. The prosecution alleges that between March and June 2017, he fraudulently obtained approximately Sh1.1 million from victims through land transactions at Ash Plaza on Biashara Street in Nairobi

Specific Area: Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company (NCWSC),
Motive: To secure employment and earn salary benefits
Case Summary: Okandah John, a former employee of the Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company, was convicted of fraud-related offences after using a forged University of Nairobi degree certificate to obtain employment in 2016. He remained on the public payroll until 2023, earning approximately Sh4.75 million in salaries.

Families of Multimedia University (MMU) students shot by police during a Monday protest are demanding the identification and interdiction of the officers responsible for firing live ammunition. The demonstrations erupted after students protested a university staff strike and the suspension of exams, accusing lecturers of refusing to administer tests despite students being prepared. The police response left at least four students seriously injured, including third-year finance student Abubakar Fugicha, who has a live bullet lodged in his esophagus, and first-year journalism student Victor Kariuki, who was shot in the back and has a bullet lodged near his spine. Civil society group Vocal Africa, led by Executive Director Hussein Khallid, strongly condemned the police's deployment of excessive force against citizens exercising their constitutional right to peaceful assembly, urging law enforcement to respect human lives and utilize non-violent crowd-control methods.

Motive: Financial gain through alleged fraudulent gold transaction
Case Summary: A senior Somali government official, Ismael Abukar Osman, was charged in Nairobi with allegedly defrauding a businessman of KSh 3.5 million through a fake gold scam. Prosecutors opposed his release on bail, arguing that he poses a flight risk and has links to ongoing terrorism-related investigations. The court ordered that he remain in custody at the Industrial Area Remand Prison pending a ruling on his bail application.

On Friday, June 12, 2026, a violent mob of approximately 200 hired individuals on motorcycles stormed the grounds of the All Saints Cathedral in Kilimani, Nairobi, forcibly disrupting an ongoing church budget review meeting. The invading group confronted security guards, overwhelmed responding police officers, and caused widespread panic, forcing congregants to flee while robbing some of their mobile phones. Order was only restored after police fired warning shots into the air. Following the incident, the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) used forensic CCTV analysis to track down and arrest key suspects in Mathare North, identifying them as members of the notorious "Chini ya Mnazi" criminal gang. Arraigned before the Kibera Law Courts, the chief magistrate ordered the suspects detained for 10 working days to allow detectives to extract mobile phone data, trace witnesses, and map out the gang's operational network. Investigations have taken a highly political turn after a suspect confessed that the group was financed by a Member of Parliament and assisted by plain-clothes officers to initially disrupt an opposition-linked meeting for a payout of Ksh 2,000 per person, prompting the Inspector General of Police to vow that no politician or officer involved will be shielded from justice.

Seven Kenyan seafarers who were detained in Tanzania on human trafficking charges since March 31 have been successfully repatriated following diplomatic intervention by Cabinet Secretary Hassan Joho. The crew of the fishing vessel FV Sea Ndovu had been sentenced by Tanzanian authorities to 10 years in prison or a fine of roughly Sh3.3 million (Tsh90 million) after being caught carrying 54 undocumented migrants from the DRC and Burundi. While the seafarers claimed they had no operational control over the illegal voyage, CS Joho ultimately paid their fines to secure their freedom after weeks of bilateral negotiations. Upon their emotional arrival at Moi International Airport, officials urged Kenyan maritime workers to strictly adhere to international maritime laws to avoid future entrapment in regional smuggling operations.

The High Court of Kenya in Nairobi, under Justice Patricia Nyaudi, has issued a landmark ruling halting the operations of Rology Medical Kenya Limited. The suspension follows a lawsuit filed by the Kenya Association of Radiologists, who alleged that the company's AI-assisted tele-radiology platform lacked sufficient oversight and unlawfully exposed and transferred sensitive patient data. In response, the court ordered the immediate cessation of the firm's activities and directed the Ministry of Health and the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council to revoke its licenses and approvals. While Rology Medical Kenya Limited has denied the allegations and defended its services, it must remain suspended until it fully complies with the nation's digital health and data protection laws.

Motive: Negligence and to evade criminal prosecution
Case Summary: Following a Peponi School leavers' dinner at Muthaiga Country Club, an Isuzu D-Max carrying five students rolled along Ngong Road at 3:50 AM. The crash killed two foreign students instantly and left a third in a coma. While the school’s headmaster and initial witness accounts indicated that a prominent businessman’s minor son was driving drunk and speeding, the family later claimed his 34-year-old cousin was behind the wheel. Alleging a high-profile cover-up by the family, the school, and local police, the comatose student's family (represented by Murgor & Murgor Advocates) has petitioned the DCI for a full forensic probe, citing text-message apologies from the minor and warning of potential diplomatic fallout.
Two rape cases from late last year remain unresolved despite happening around the same area. The detectives in charge of the case are cracking on protest planners.

There has been a rising matter of foreign nationals acquiring the Kenyan IDs and passports after bribing some officials at the registry and immigration departments. Several cases of Somali nationals holding Kenyan IDs have been highlighted.

Specific Area: Upper Imenti Forest, Nkunga crater lake
Motive: Convenience and reckless waste disposal due to easy roadside access
Case Summary: The Imenti Forest in Meru County is currently under severe ecological threat from both human pollution and commercial development. Long celebrated as a serene recreational space and a vital wildlife sanctuary for elephants and monkeys, the forest is increasingly marred by the illegal, large-scale dumping of soiled baby diapers along major traversing roads. This waste, often dumped deliberately in large sacks, emits foul odors, ruins the area's therapeutic value, and threatens to contaminate critical river catchments that feed into major national water sources. Simultaneously, environmental groups like Rhino Ark are fiercely opposing a government proposal to excise over 100 acres of this protected land for a state lodge, golf course, and airstrip. Activists and the National Environment Management Authority (Nema) are urging a halt to these development plans—suggesting safer alternatives like upgrading nearby existing airstrips—to prevent irreversible damage to a critical water tower and biodiversity hotspot.

A businessman and family administrator, Twahir Salim Swod, has accused security officers of executing an illegal midnight raid on a disputed beachfront property in Kilifi County. Armed with rifles and driving official vehicles, the officers stormed the property on a Friday night, arrested Swod and several workers, and held them in custody at the Malindi Police Station. While the victims were detained, the property's structures were torched and business equipment was looted and loaded onto a pickup truck. Following his release, Swod discovered that solar panels, batteries, life jackets, and other items valued at approximately Sh5 million were missing, leaving behind only burnt tents and mattresses. The family claims the raid stems from an ongoing land dispute, alleging that workers from a hotel linked to the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) have previously issued threats. Swod has officially called for an independent investigation into the incident.

Geoffrey Kimongo, a former political advisor of governer  John Mruttu,Kimonge was arrested and charged with fraud,for emblezzling funds from the county government to enrich himself.The amount that he fraudently acquired sums up to sh12,458,990,the court ordered him to pay back the money.

Specific Area: Jua Kali area,Cabo Delgado region, northern Mozambique (intended final destination)
Motive: Expanding an emerging Islamic State (ISIS) recruitment network
Case Summary: Two Kenyan nationals, Yusuf Mbashir Swaleh and Abdulkarim Mohamed Salim, were intercepted by Tanzanian authorities at the Horohoro border point while allegedly trying to travel to the conflict-ridden Cabo Delgado region in northern Mozambique. Following their arrest, Kenyan security agencies launched an investigation into a cross-border recruitment pipeline linking Kenyan youths to ISIS cells. Charged under Kenya's Prevention of Terrorism Act, Swaleh is accused of funding Salim’s travel via an Sh8,000 mobile money transfer and possessing radical material on a Samsung smartphone, while Salim allegedly organized recruitment meetings in Mombasa. The Anti-Terror Police Unit (ATPU) successfully opposed their bail in a Kwale court, arguing that the suspects lack stable income, possess valid passports, have ties to associates in Mozambique, and present a high flight risk through porous regional borders.

A dispute arose in Kasigau Location, Taita-Taveta County, after residents complained that herders from a neighbouring county were repeatedly driving camels into private farms and settlement areas in search of water and pasture. Angry farmers protested at the Voi Police Station, accusing authorities of failing to act and alleging collusion with the herders.

About 30 armed attackers stormed Chemelil Sugar Academy in Kisumu County as students returned from the half-term break. The gang forced its way through the school gate, assaulted teachers, parents, workers, and security personnel, vandalized offices, and stole cash, mobile phones, and other valuables. Many victims fled into surrounding sugarcane plantations to escape the attack. At least 10 people, including teachers, a parent, the bursar, and a supplier, were injured,

Motive: Negligence and poor waste management practices
Case Summary: The ecological deterioration of Lake Victoria has severely disrupted Kisumu City with an invasive, foul-smelling stench caused by a combination of climate change and human pollution. Local businesses and residents are dumping sewage, plastics, and agricultural runoff into the lake's feeding rivers, overloading the water with excess nutrients. This nutrient buildup fuels massive algal blooms which, upon dying and decomposing, deplete oxygen levels and release noxious gases like hydrogen sulphide. As a result, the Kisumu Water and Sanitation Company (Kiwasco) has been forced to reduce water production and ramp up chemical treatments, causing widespread supply shortages, while public health officials warn of rising health risks like nausea, headaches, and skin irritation.

Motive: Speculated attempts to skew the upcoming local by-election by bringing in non-resident individuals
Case Summary: Tension flared up in Kaimbaga Ward, Ol Kalou constituency, ahead of a highly anticipated July 16 by-election, after local residents intercepted and surrounded school buses suspected of being involved in electoral malpractice. Angry locals blocked the vehicles and forced the passengers to alight before chasing them away, driven by allegations that the buses were transporting individuals involved in an illegal national identity card auction scheme to influence the upcoming vote. The confrontation, recorded and widely shared on social media, has intensified regional political friction and fueled speculation pointing towards UDA party involvement. While local UDA leaders—who recently campaigned for candidate Samuel Muchina Nyaga—have completely dismissed allegations of importing outsiders and accused critics of discrediting the IEBC, security agencies have yet to issue an official statement clarifying the true nature and destination of the buses

A violent political clash erupted at Umoja Senior School in Kuresoi North, Nakuru County, during a youth empowerment rally, prompting police to launch a manhunt for the area MP, Alfred Mutai. The confrontation began when MP Mutai, accompanied by roughly 200 supporters, attempted to enter the venue but was blocked by youth groups allegedly allied with Nakuru Governor Susan Kihika. As the situation quickly escalated into chaos, police report that MP Mutai drew his personal firearm and shot into the crowd in self-defense, injuring three civilians. Following the clashes, which also resulted in the torching of a minibus and heavy vandalism of several vehicles, authorities arrested 56 suspects at the MP’s residence and recovered an assortment of crude weapons alongside spent ammunition. While MP Mutai denies shooting anyone and blames Governor Kihika for mobilizing outside youth to trigger the violence, security agencies are under pressure to conduct impartial investigations into both political factions involved.

John Makokha witnessed a chaotic scene at a recent burial in Matungu where the peaceful mourning process was completely disrupted by political goons. Groups of youth aligned with rival political factions invaded the funeral while chanting political slogans and wearing distinct regalia to identify their allegiances. Makokha noted that these youth marched aggressively through the crowd, shouting, carrying crude weapons, and physically pushing mourners aside. These youths were moving in large numbers, dressed in matching or intimidating outfits (such as specific buttons, scarves, or colored regalia to identify themselves with different political factions). The atmosphere became so hostile and unpredictable that helpless residents felt entirely powerless to stop them, highlighting the growing trend of politicians weaponizing funerals for aggressive political mobilization.

Residents, matatu operators, and traders in Migori staged a protest over prolonged government delays in repairing the structurally compromised Migori Footbridge on the Sirare–Sare A1 Road. The demonstrators blocked a key diversion route, severely disrupting transit and commercial business operations along the busy Migori–Isebania highway. Migori Bus Park chairman Jared Oketch noted that the community resorted to demonstrations after exhausting all formal avenues to seek government intervention for the bridge, which developed severe structural weaknesses back in February and forced motorists onto lengthy alternative routes. While local operators have vowed to sustain weekly protests until physical rehabilitation begins, Public Investments Principal Secretary Cyrell Wagunda stated that the government is currently working to secure the necessary funds to repair the infrastructure.

Specific Area: Kwa Njoroge village near City Park
Case Summary: On a Friday night, residents of Kwa Njoroge village—an informal settlement near Nairobi's City Park—faced a violent eviction attempt by armed men accompanied by police officers. The attackers, allegedly acting on behalf of a private developer who claims ownership of the land, invaded the settlement with pangas, guns, and teargas, forcing sleeping families from their homes and assaulting an elderly resident. The community, many of whom have lived there for decades, successfully repulsed the attackers and subsequently staged protests demanding government intervention and transparency. While residents maintain this was an illegal and forceful land grab involving measly compensation offers of Sh3,000, an anonymous police officer defended the nighttime raid as a lawful execution of a court order against residents who had allegedly refused to vacate after being paid.
A fire broke out in Gikomba market killing 2 people and massive destruction of business. Traders fear that the fires are deliberately set to facilitate land grabbing.

49 young people have been killed by police between January and May 2026 with the recent fuel protests leaving 24 dead. This is according to Social Justice Centre Working Group and other Human Rights Groups' data.

An audit by Auditor-General Nancy Gathungu for the year ended June 30, 2025, has exposed widespread human resource and payroll fraud within Governor Lati Lelelit’s Samburu County Government. The report reveals that between July 2024 and June 2025, at least 83 employees were paid millions of shillings despite having no designated job titles, roles, or clear deployment, with some personnel records missing vital biodata or sharing duplicate national ID numbers. Furthermore, the administration illegally spent Sh60 million on an unapproved "Governor’s Delivery Unit" containing 29 staff hired completely outside the County Public Service Board's jurisdiction and without any legal due process. Compounding these severe compliance failures, the county bypassed National Treasury regulations by paying Sh59.4 million in salaries completely outside the standard Integrated Payroll and Personnel Database (IPPD) and unlawfully deducted Sh2.7 million in taxes from employees with disabilities who were legally exempt, prompting urgent calls for systemic corrective action to safeguard public funds.

Motive: Vested interests and elite networks using a secretive, investor-led framework to bypass public accountability
Case Summary: A new report by Transparency International (TI) Kenya, titled Corruption Risk Assessment of Infrastructure Projects in Kenya, reveals that the country is facing a massive debt burden due to critical governance failures and high corruption risks embedded in the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) project. Assessed between September 2025 and March 2026, the SGR received a staggering vulnerability score of 4.49 out of 5 using the Infrastructure Corruption Risk Assessment Tool (ICRAT). This systemic lack of due diligence caused the original 539 billion Shilling loan—heavily sourced from Chinese lenders—to balloon to 737.5 billion Shillings by late 2024 due to accumulated interest from delayed repayments. The report flags that the project was pushed through via an opaque, investor-led process that cut out public participation, limited parliamentary oversight, and hid final contract costs. Furthermore, highly restrictive clauses locked any dispute resolutions into arbitration in Beijing while enforcing strict confidentiality. TI Kenya warns that the country loses over 600 billion Shillings annually to stalled or mismanaged infrastructure, and urges the government to enforce strict transparency and proactive documentation before proceeding with planned SGR extensions to Malaba.

A 21-year-old Thika Technical Training Institute student, Elizabeth Ngina, was found murdered in a rented room in Kiang’ombe Estate, Thika, Kiambu County. The body showed signs of extreme violence, including beheading, missing fingers, and approximately 32 stab wounds to the back.According to police reports, the victim was allegedly in a relationship with the suspect, who has since been arrested.

A man identified as Charles Paya was arrested in Ndhiwa Sub-County, Homa Bay County, for exhuming the body of his first wife, Agnes Otieno, shortly after her burial. The body had initially been buried at his homestead following her death.However, due to prior disputes and personal differences, Paya reportedly objected to her burial at the family home and preferred that she be buried in a maize plantation outside the compound. A few days after the burial, Paya, with the assistance of his son, exhumed the body and reburied it in a grave dug in a maize farm.Police investigations revealed that the action was driven by longstanding disagreements between Paya and his first wife, as well as tensions arising from his remarriage. Authorities are now handling the case as an unlawful exhumation and improper handling of human remains.

The case concerns Kenya’s Health Cabinet Secretary, Aden Duale, who was found guilty of contempt of court for allowing continued construction of an Ebola isolation facility at Laikipia Air Base in Nanyuki, despite court orders halting the project.The High Court had issued conservatory orders suspending the implementation of the project, which is backed by the United States as part of Ebola preparedness efforts. However, construction activities reportedly continued, prompting legal action by petitioners.After being found in contempt, Mr. Duale appeared before the court for mitigation. He apologised, explaining that he had misunderstood the court’s orders, believing they only applied to the Kenya–US collaboration aspect and not to Kenya’s independent public health actions.
