Specific Area: Nairobi (161), Kajiado (123), Kiambu (36), Murang'a (12), Bungoma (9), Meru (6), Laikipia (5), and Machakos (3).
Motive: To commemorate the second anniversary of the Gen-Zs who were killed during the 25th June, 2024 Nationwide Anti-Finance bill protests
Case Summary: During the Gen Z anniversary demonstrations in Kenya, security forces arrested at least 355 people nationwide, with Nairobi County recording the highest number of detentions. Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen stated that those arrested would face charges ranging from robbery and vandalism to road obstruction. Among those targeted by police were activists, grieving families of past protest victims—such as Gillian Munyao, mother of the late Rex Masai—and former Chief Justice David Maraga, who were accosted by armed officers while attempting to peacefully march to the Parliament Buildings. Former CJ Maraga strongly condemned the state's deployment of excessive force, accusing the government of trying to evade accountability for the 65 deaths from the previous anti-Finance Bill protests and calling on President William Ruto to issue a public apology and ensure justice is served.

Specific Area: Landhies Road and various major roadways leading into the central business district of Nairobi, Kenya
Motive: To commemorate the second anniversary of the historic Gen Z protest killings by State security forces and continue pushing anti-government grievances
Case Summary: The state arraigned more than 100 protesters at the Milimani Law Courts following their arrests during the June 25, 2026, Gen Z anniversary demonstrations. The protests, organized to mark two years since more than 60 people were killed by State security agents, resulted in a wave of arrests across Nairobi, with suspects processed through major stations including Kamukunji, Shauri Moyo, Industrial Area, and Central. The prosecution alleged that the demonstrators unlawfully assembled and intentionally gridlocked traffic on Landhies Road using stones and burning tires. Conversely, the defense team countered that the gridlock was entirely manufactured by police roadblocks that locked down the city. While all arraigned suspects pleaded not guilty, the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) dropped all charges against a young mother who had been brought into the courtroom holding her toddler, evoking an emotional response from onlookers.

Specific Area: Chief's area at Kona Mbuta, Manyatta
Case Summary: Police in Kisumu are investigating the brutal sexual assault and murder of an unidentified middle-aged woman whose body was discovered in the Kona Mbuta area of Manyatta. Local residents reported that the victim, a mother who had left her home to seek casual work, appeared to have fought her attackers before she was raped and killed. The shocking incident has caused uproar, spreading fear among local women and sparking renewed demands for heightened security in the region as DCI detectives work to track down the assailants.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) has launched a crackdown in Mombasa against rogue developers who are illegally adding extra floors to buildings without regulatory approval. According to NCA Compliance Manager Stephen Mwilu, an enforcement operation resulted in the arrest of a developer who breached a seven-storey limit, highlighting a dangerous trend where builders ignore suspension orders and compromise public safety. The authority has linked these unauthorized extensions to past building collapses and warned that non-compliant projects will remain shut down, with offenders facing stiff penalties of up to Sh3 million in fines, three years of imprisonment, or both.

Specific Area: Parliament Buildings,Central Police Station, Parklands, and Ngong Road
Case Summary: Seven human rights activists experienced a harrowing 48-hour ordeal after being abducted by plain-clothes police officers outside the Parliament Buildings during a memorial event marking the second anniversary of the Gen Z protests. The activists were bundled into a police truck and later transferred into the boots of three Subaru Outbacks by masked, armed men who drove them to an undisclosed location. During their secret detention, they were stripped of their phones, locked in separate rooms, and subjected to severe beatings while being aggressively interrogated about who was funding their protests to embarrass the President and the Kenya Kwanza administration. Following their release, several of the victims required urgent admission to Nairobi Women's Hospital for extensive injuries, drawing fierce condemnation from civil society organisations like the Kenya Human Rights Commission, which called out the state for violating citizens' constitutional rights.

Motive: Targeted intimidation linked to The Standard Group's editorial stance
Case Summary: Four armed men brandishing AK-47 rifles attempted to abduct Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich along Mercy Njeri-Mastoo Road in Nakuru. The attackers used a Probox to overtake and block Kiprotich's vehicle, but he managed to lock his doors and swiftly swerve away to escape after one of the gunmen momentarily closed a passenger door. According to his lawyer, Gordon Ogola, the incident followed a pattern of suspicious surveillance involving a Subaru, and he strongly linked the attempted kidnapping to state-driven intimidation following harsh public criticism from President William Ruto regarding the media house's editorial stance. In response, leadership from The Standard Group and the Kenya Union of Journalists (KUJ) condemned the attack as a direct assault on press freedom, declaring they would not be intimidated while demanding a transparent investigation from authorities.
